body:
`TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` (`internal/gateway/wsl_test.go`) fails 3 of 3 on main c158b0439 with go1.27.2 darwin/arm64, and passes 3 of 3 there with go1.26.8 (go.mod's, CI's). I couldn't find it filed. #3547 and #3549 are the other Go 1.27 reds from the same run.

```
--- FAIL: TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback (10.03s)
    wsl_test.go:165: WSL network gone: http://[::1]:58208/ answers = true
```

Run, in a sandbox HOME at c158b0439 with nothing else changed:

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=local   go test -tags nogui -count=3 -run '^TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback$' ./internal/gateway/   # go1.27.2: FAIL
GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 go test -tags nogui -count=3 -run '^TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback$' ./internal/gateway/   # ok
```

**Likely cause, checked once:** `answers()` makes a new `http.Client` with no Transport, so every probe goes through `http.DefaultTransport` and its pool of kept-alive connections. After "WSL network up", the pool holds a connection to `[::1]:port`. Closing the WSL listener doesn't close connections it has already accepted, so the "WSL network gone" probe is answered over that connection, and on Go 1.27 it holds for the whole 10s wait. With only the probe changed to `&http.Client{Timeout: time.Second, Transport: &http.Transport{DisableKeepAlives: true}}`, the test passes 3 of 3 on go1.27.2. Not checked: what changed between 1.26 and 1.27 to make the old connection last the wait.
title: TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback is red on Go 1.27: its probe reuses a kept-alive connection after the WSL listener closes
